text: People all over the world cried over this train station.
And the story they cried about wasn't true.
It's called Kyushirataki.
It's in a tiny town in Hokkaido, Japan.
No staff, one short platform, almost nobody around.
A high school girl named Kanaharada used it every morning.
She stood on that quiet platform, a train came, and it took her to school.
Then a post went viral. It said the station was supposed to close years ago.
But the railway company found out about her and kept it open, just for her.
And they'd close it the day she graduated.
And that's exactly what happened.
Kanah graduated in March 2016.
The station closed in March 2016.
News channels around the world ran the story.
People called it the kindest thing a railway ever did.
But wait, before I tell you what really happened, follow this page on Instagram and subscribe here.
Because the real story is stranger than the viral one. And most videos never tell it.
You see, the railway never kept that station open for her.
In July 2015, months before the story went viral,
the railway company announced it was closing four stations on that line.
The reason was boring, almost nobody used them.
And the date? In Japan, train timetables change every March.
March is also when the school year ends.
Two things landed in the same month and the internet drew a line between them.
There's more. She wasn't riding an empty train.
When she got on, dozens of passengers were already inside,
mostly students from her own school.
And she said the station simply let her sleep a little longer in the morning.
So the station wasn't saved for her.
It was closing quietly, like many small stations do.
She was just the person still using it.
That October, the building was torn down.
The sweet story was never true, but a lot of people believed it anyway.
So the station that stayed open for one girl never stayed open for her at all.
Here's what I can't figure out. If it was never true, why did so many of us believe it so fast?
Tell me in the comments, I really want to know.
